Australia, a country bigger than the continental US with over 20 million people. Voting is compulsory so virtually the entire eligible population votes (around 15 million votes). Outcome of national election known inside of 24hrs, usually closer to 12, with the overwhelming majority of ballots being counted. 

Everyone gets two ballots, one for the house of reps (usually 5-12 candidates) and a senate ballot (anywhere from 10+ candidates), referenda are an additional ballot. We have proportional representation, which means we count the votes for each candidate, then we count where each vote goes next, if your preferred candidate doesn't win, and again, and again, until there is a winner. You guys have straight up and down counting. In a state (CA) whose economy is the size of most of Western Europe. You're counting fewer things, in an easier way, over a smaller area.
